URL debug date is reset after entry; native time then advances normally. Sampling never freezes or accelerates the page clock.

reverseOrderRecheck.purpose: One bounded counterbalanced pair for both viewport cases following isolated initial renderSubmit tails; preserve initial observations rather than selecting a preferred run.

performance.limits: Two runs per case per version across initial before-after and recheck after-before rounds, native clock, software renderer with CPU4x. Samples do not establish global absence of regressions. Render elapsed time is main-thread/driver submission timing, not GPU completion or physical device FPS. No speedup claim.
performance.qualificationMeaning: Frame-count/window, matching quality/DPR, resource stability and browser error checks only; not a before-after latency non-regression verdict.
performance.verdict: Resource budgets verified; latency conclusion limited. Both desktop versions exhibited isolated native submit stalls. The cause remains unlocated and a latency regression is not ruled out by these samples.

method.clock: Native Date/performance/RAF, no freezing or timewarp
method.defaults: Production HTML/assets, natural time/weather and adaptive quality; no debugEnv or seeded storage
method.audio: Native AudioContext/AudioParam/source and HTMLAudioElement forwarding; targets, playback and allocation observed without replacing audio
method.resources: Native WebGL create/delete counts and native audio allocation/source snapshots; no renderer settings changed
method.isolation: New browser context per view; no personal drafts or editor visited; no reload
method.evidence: Room and reading screenshots only; physical listening, speaker/headphone quality, real mobile hardware and Safari are outside this run
method.loss: WEBGL_lose_context on the existing production canvas, then the actual fallback reader
